text.p: - Granting Chechnya free economic zone status would not only legalise the de facto existing situation but also extend the tax and duty free regime of the "special territory".
- Belarus President Alexander Lukashenko may try to play the Russian card in the run-up to the referendum on a new Belarus constitution when he takes the floor in the Duma on Wednesday.
- Poor tax collection makes it unlikely Russia will obtain the delayed October tranche of the IMF loan.
- No Russian financial institution is likely to be able to splash out on the soon to be floated giant Agroprombank and political considerations may come into play.
- The State Duma debates the Law on the Government today which it plans to use to undermine the powers of the presidential administration.
- Russia, Turkmenistan and Iran insist on their right to drill for oil throughout the Caspian Sea.
- Abkhaz separatist president Vladislav Ardzinba says war in his republic vying for independence from Georgia could flare again.
- The ideas of accord and conciliation between different social groups in Russia could take root only if they are backed by strong economic performance.
- Chechen separatists are trying to blackmail Russia into paying for the damage done to the rebel republic during the 21-month-long conflict.
